title: Does R(k,l+1) - R(k,l) have a meaningful asymptotic formula for fixed k

problemStatement.formal: \text{Fix } k \ge 3. \text{ Determine whether } \Delta_l(k) := R(k,l+1) - R(k,l) \text{ satisfies } \Delta_l(k) \sim g_k(l) \text{ for some explicit } g_k \text{ as } l \to \infty.
problemStatement.plain: For a fixed first argument k, look at how much the Ramsey number R(k,l) jumps when l increases by one: the increment R(k,l+1) - R(k,l). This question asks whether that increment has a clean asymptotic formula (some explicit function g_k(l) it is asymptotically equal to) rather than growing erratically as l grows.
whyMatters: An asymptotic for the increment is strictly stronger than the ratio-convergence statement of Erdős Problem #1014: it pins down the local growth rate of the Ramsey function, not just that it grows smoothly.
It would sharply constrain any conjectured closed form for R(k,l); for k=3 the expectation is Δ_l(3) ~ c·l/log l, matching R(3,l) ~ c·l²/log l.
It connects Ramsey growth to finite-difference/discrete-derivative techniques and gives a concrete quantitative target often easier to attack than a full closed-form asymptotic.

proven: Erdős–Szekeres upper bound R(k,l) ≤ C(k+l-2, k-1), giving polynomial growth O(l^{k-1}) for fixed k (diagonal_ramsey_upper).
Recurrence R(k,l+1) ≤ R(k,l) + R(k-1,l+1), hence increment bound Δ_l(k) ≤ R(k-1,l+1); for k=3, Δ_l(3) ≤ l+1 (increment_bound_general, increment_bound_k3).
Tight order of magnitude R(3,l) = Θ(l²/log l) from AKS upper and Kim/Shearer lower bounds (R3_asymptotic_bounds).
open: Whether Δ_l(3) = R(3,l+1) - R(3,l) has an asymptotic formula (conjecturally ~ c·l/log l); open because the implied constants in the Θ(l²/log l) bounds differ.
Whether any explicit g_k(l) describes Δ_l(k) for fixed k ≥ 4, where even the order of magnitude of R(k,l) is unknown.
Whether the increment is monotone or eventually smooth in l rather than oscillating.
knownResults.goal: Formalize the structural consequences: prove that a power-law asymptotic R(k,l) ~ c_k·l^{k-1}/(log l)^{k-2} would force Δ_l(k) ~ (k-1)·c_k·l^{k-2}/(log l)^{k-2}, and relate this increment asymptotic to the already-formalized ratio and difference reformulations of Erdős #1014.

insights: The consecutive increment of a sequence is provably NOT a function of its asymptotic (~) equivalence class: witness u l = l, v l = l + (-1)^l have v/u -> 1 (u ~ v) yet increment ratio (v(l+1)-v l)/(u(l+1)-u l) = 1 - 2(-1)^l does not converge (=-1 on evens, =3 on odds). This is the rigorous form of the prose sin-based caution and formally justifies why the naive power-law Approach A is invalid.

Adding the base sequence u its own o(u)-scale (normalized-increment) regularity does NOT rescue increment-ratio convergence; asymptotic equivalence + first-order smoothness of u together are still insufficient, so the honest increment-ratio bridge is unavoidable

The ratio→1 hypothesis of #1014 is not merely a local (one-step) statement: it forces GLOBAL subexponential growth R(k,l)=e^{o(l)}, i.e. R(k,l)^{1/l}→1. Mechanism is the ratio-test⇒root-test passage made rigorous through Cesàro averaging of log-increments — distinct from the increment/gap/reciprocal bridges already in the file. Consistent with (but derived without) the polynomial rate R(3,l)=Θ(l²/log l).

Closure of the ratio-convergence class (researcher-6): the class {R : R(l+1)/R(l)→1} is scale-invariant (c·R has an IDENTICAL ratio sequence for c≠0), shift-invariant (R(·+s) preserves the limit), and closed under pointwise PRODUCTS (ratio→1·1) and real POWERS R^p (ratio→1^p). So #1014s hypothesis is a genuine tail/normalization-invariant property (regular variation of index 0), independent of the scale of R — orthogonal to all prior increment/log-increment/gap/reciprocal/root-test bridges, which analyse a single fixed sequence.

Sum-closure completes the ratio-convergence-class algebra: the class {R : R(l+1)/R(l)→1} is closed under pointwise ADDITION for EVENTUALLY-POSITIVE sequences (ratio_tendsto_one_add, Erdos1014OQ03.lean). Unlike scale/shift/product/power, sum needs positivity: the ratio of R+S is a convex combination of the two ratios (weights R/(R+S), S/(R+S)), squeezed to 1 by |(R+S)(l+1)/(R+S)l − 1| ≤ |aR−1|+|aS−1|→0 (per-term |ΔR/(R+S)| ≤ |ΔR/R| = |aR−1| since R≤R+S). So the class is a POSITIVE CONE closed under + and ·. ★abs_add renamed→abs_add_le; per-term denom-bound via one_div_le_one_div_of_le + mul_one_div (avoid fragile div_le_div_of_nonneg_left); squeeze_zero_norm' for the ∀ᶠ bound; (hR.sub_const 1).abs then simpa for |aR−1|→0.
